expectations.basis: S7 L01, blind labellers agreed. G: It asks whether each named product is only an example or shared infrastructure; the true and false criteria make the same distinction by asking whether the section sends the agent into that product's own workflow. H: It asks one yes/no proposition: whether every product the section routes into is only a labelled example or shared infrastructure. The criteria supply the corresponding allowed and disallowed cases.

S7 L01, blind labellers agreed. G: The instruction asks whether products are named only as examples or shared infrastructure, and the criteria distinguish those cases from product-specific commands, procedures, or state files. H: The instruction asks whether routed products are examples or shared infrastructure; the true and false criteria distinguish those cases from instructions to use a product's own workflow.

S7 L03, independent settlement: The standard begins 'A Noul', but the source explicitly declares this question's type as 'choice' and supplies the categorical answers 'none', 'condition' and 'work'. I follow labeler_g because this entry falls outside that Noul-specific standard; labeler_h's assessment of the categorical question does not establish applicability.

S7 L03, independent settlement: The instruction asks 'Which part does the branch leave out?', and the criteria answer with both parts present, a condition that 'can't be observed', or observable condition but missing or unchanged work. I follow labeler_h because these criteria classify the same branch gap the instruction asks about; this standard says 'A question' and does not restrict itself to Nouls, so labeler_g's type-based exclusion does not apply.

S7 L06, blind labellers agreed. G: It asks whether guidance states a positive target instead of only what to avoid; both criteria branches decide that one distinction, including an actionable skill handoff as a positive target. H: It asks one observable yes/no question: whether guidance gives a positive target instead of only naming what to avoid. The criteria distinguish positive actions or targets from avoidance-only guidance.

S7 L06, blind labellers agreed. G: The instruction's positive-target test matches the criteria: true names an action, target, or useful handoff, while false only names prohibitions and leaves the target unknown. H: The criteria answer whether guidance gives an action/target or only an avoidance, matching the instruction's positive-target question.

S7 L09, blind labellers agreed. G: It asks whether a rule transfers to materially different repositories, stacks, or teams; the criteria define transferable versus single-case judgments on that same proposition. H: It asks one observable proposition: whether the rule's judgment transfers to materially different repositories, stacks, or teams. The criteria describe transferable and case-specific judgments.

S7 L09, blind labellers agreed. G: The instruction's transfer test matches the criteria's distinction between general judgments and a particular product, path, stack, or incident stated as universal. H: The criteria define transferability using the instruction's cases: examples or adopted scope can transfer, while a single product-specific case stated as universal cannot.
